issues.description: Method getTotalNumberOfStudents: the problem statement and UML declare a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, and the template's TODO asks students to add that method without parameters. The solution implementation declares getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) (a different parameter list) and internally calls getTotalNumberOfStudents(true). This parameter mismatch between the problem/UML/template and the solution will confuse students about the expected API and which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem statement and UML by changing the solution method signature to: public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() and implement it to return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. Update all internal calls (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to call the no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents(). Alternatively (if the intended design requires the boolean parameter), update the problem statement, UML diagram and template TODOs to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) so all artifacts match.

issues.description: Concept: total number of students. The problem statement and UML require a no-argument method named getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning an int. The template contains a TODO placeholder for the getTotalNumberOfStudents method but does not provide a signature. The solution implements a method with the different identifier and signature getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests): int (adds a boolean parameter named includeGuests). This name/signature mismatch means students cannot unambiguously map the required API from the problem/UML to the provided solution; they may implement a no-arg method while the solution shows a parameterized variant (or vice versa), and automated tests or graders expecting the no-arg signature could fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Make the solution provide the no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students as specified in the UML/problem. If optional inclusion of guest students is desired, add an overloaded method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) in addition to the no-arg method, and update the problem statement/UML/tests to document the overload. Alternatively, update the UML and problem text to explicitly require getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) and update the template accordingly so all artifacts use the same signature.
